hook: A society can have enough food and still leave people hungry.
readerPromise: Examine the physical and institutional conditions of universal sufficiency while distinguishing it from unlimited abundance.
protectedRevelations: The author’s final feasibility verdict, timeline and policy prescriptions

End with a lived home or shared meal as the concrete aspiration, presented as a question rather than an achieved forecast.

notes: Replaced material-floor and hopeful-material-argument phrasing with ordinary needs, access and maintenance. Kept conditional investigation rather than promising a guaranteed abundance date.
Every spoken sentence independently checked against the canonical English source for clear purpose, intended viewer response, source fidelity and natural spoken wording.

sentenceIntentions.text: A society can have enough food and still leave people hungry.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Open with the difference between supply and access.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Recognize why more production alone may not end hunger.

sentenceIntentions.text: Enough for Everyone asks how basic needs could become secure without pretending resources are endless.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Name the book and bounded ambition.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Understand that the proposal concerns basic needs within finite resources.

sentenceIntentions.text: The book examines what it takes to provide energy, water, food, housing, and essential care.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Picture the essentials a secure life requires.

sentenceIntentions.text: New technology can expand what is possible, but someone still has to build, maintain, and share it.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Connect technology to work and institutions.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: See why possibility does not automatically become availability.

sentenceIntentions.text: A house that exists is not much help to a person who cannot afford to live there.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Ground access in an everyday example.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Feel the human gap between a full inventory and a usable home.

sentenceIntentions.text: Time, attention, and the places everyone wants remain a different kind of problem.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Keep the promise honest about remaining scarcity.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Understand why abundance cannot satisfy every desire.

sentenceIntentions.text: The book offers a hopeful question with practical difficulties still in view.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Offer the emotional shape of the reading.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Feel room for hope without being asked to ignore difficulties.

sentenceIntentions.text: What would have to change for having enough to mean that everyone can actually use it?
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Want to explore the path from physical capacity to shared access.
